items.note: Story 1: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose president 1889-1911, creamery built 1891.
Article VII quoted verbatim including the governing-station clause.
Story-1 title 'the rule that turned a figure into money' plus 'made the butterfat test, not the pound of milk, the measure of a man's month'.
Effie Loomis secretary 1901 with the minute book; Teague bookkeeper 1905; Sill buttermaker.
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager 1913-1938; nephew explicitly rejected.

Station-gain line quoted with shape (credited vs received, 3,040 lb, five and a quarter per cent, carried to the general account) and the 1898 entry printed; the 1905-vs-1898 origin is left unresolved but the line's core fact is stated.
Seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass 'borrowed of Larrow Green'.

Weighed at intake, ten-day composite jars, charged by pipette, hand tester, cream down / skim home. The reading-as-percent-on-the-graduated-neck detail appears only in Section F, but the core mechanics are in A.
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897 (1 May 1898 rejected).
Full invoice transcribed: 6 doz. pipettes 17.6 c.c., 12 doz. bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 3: gap 'the same in February as in July, flat as a floor' and 'the true effect, 0.19' - flatness plus the figure, both inside Section A.

Not in Section A. The claim that the pipette is the one instrument that cannot be checked without a burette (and there was none in the county) appears only in Section F; Section A gives only 'the state issued burettes to field men in 1921'. Credit does not travel into A from F.
Born 1861, tester from the opening 4 May 1896 through 1924 = twenty-nine seasons; dismissed 30 April 1925; died February 1934.
Bench routine given in full in Story 2; test book identified as Keddie's, 4 May 1896-31 December 1924. Column list and crossed-and-initialed corrections not in A, but the item's core is present.
Both figures: 1896 average 3.80 on borrowed glass; 3.61 from 1898 and within three hundredths every year after (averages leaf).
8 May 1911 break, borrowed measure to 10 July, nine weeks, 3.80 through the interval, back to 3.61, Keddie's '? - A.K.'
Married Orra Brant, Emmet's sister; 'the tester was brother-in-law to the patron who lost the most'.

1919 circular is present, but the second bolded element - Keddie's statement that he tested as he was taught and cannot say why the figures are what they are - appears only in Section F. Section A quotes only the 'never taken a pound of cream' clause, which is unbolded context.
Died February 1934 still under suspicion; test book to the Ordell County Historical Rooms 1959 (and held at the office 1925-1959).
Hessel Bottom wet meadow, six farms with rights (Effie's seven rejected), Emmet Brant the largest.
Private weigh book from 1 January 1897, his scale beside the station's, 'the two columns agreed for thirty years'.
March 1902 talk that Hollow milk 'did not test with the rest'. The two gaps are kept strictly apart: 0.17 is named as the Larrow Green (3.78) comparison, 0.19 as the true shortfall (C1b, E22).
1908 committee of three under Nyle Grigg, sampling January-February-March, hay blamed - reported as the committee's finding and then defeated, not asserted.

1910 leaf: 200,000 lb even on a test of 3.42. Proportionality of the error stated in A ('every test read one part in twenty low'); the richer-herds-lost-more illustration is in D2/F, which is unbolded context.
Passed to Roy 1929; lent to Ivy 1958 ('lent, and I want the word'); to Hazel at Roy's death 1962.
Alder Corners Cheese Company, over Redlow Ridge, Vessey County, Jerome Cudd. Year does not gate.
From 1915, four of the six Hessel Bottom men over the ridge in the summer flush, Ostrey Hollow the rest of the year.
REQUIRED line met with three of four: another county (Vessey), his own new glass, and a book never compared with anyone's.
Same four men, sixteen season averages 3.78-3.82, mean 3.80, wet years and dry, 1915-1930, against the station's 3.61 - Ivy's 'fourteen' rejected.
Presented as one of 'three facts [that] defeat the hay' - same men, same wet ground, same summers, different building; and Story 5 uses Rosalie's vat ('cheese is a witness') to kill watering.
Rosalie named as Jerome's daughter (niece rejected); her copied Alder Corners figures listed among the five record sets Ivy brought together in 1958; sixteen seasons stated.

Merle Strawn, inspector with a circuit book, active from 1907 (the contested start year, correct against the planted 1908). The 1936 end-year appears only in Section F; the item's discriminating content is in A.
Lactometer on every visit from 1907, never found added water, told the manager so in 1919.
12 June 1923, run against his burette, 'Condemned the lot, the whole crate of them' - 12 July, 1922 and 1921 all rejected.
'did not weigh what it has cost them'; the office treated it 'as a broken window'; nobody drew the inference.
Order 28 June, Ammon reply 2 July, new glass in use July 1923, 1924 average 3.80 (3.90 and 3.85 rejected), nobody connected the rise.
Crate up the ladder into the loft over the intake room; Strawn's 1923 notebook found at the Farland library where the state dairy office sent the set in 1947.
Petition of January 1925 with Emmet Brant's name on it.
Board of three under Alonzo Frick; first session 17 March 1925 at Ashlin, second and third in the station's own weigh room; award 4 May.
Water (Vose), cream theft (Teague), wet hay (the 1908 report read in) - 'None was accepted.'
Four exhibits named, including Strawn's 1923 circuit notebook, with 'no one laid the second beside the fourth and looked'.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 four days before the award; 4 May, 'finds no cause established', $3,800.00 'without admission, to be charged to the station account' ($3,500 rejected).

'one-fifth of the loss' in Story 7 and '$19,000 ... five times the award' in Story 8; the award charged to the station account, the same account Story 6 shows carrying the station-gain line. The irony is not spelled out but both halves are inside Section A.
Ivy Keddie, Ansel's granddaughter, Duncan's daughter, b. 1931, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland; Vaught named with Bulletin 471.
'She brought the five record sets into one room' - test book, Brant book, Alder Corners figures, Strawn's notebook, Association ledgers.
February 1958, station loft under a tarpaulin, nine pipettes unbroken (office and 'eleven' both rejected).
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, nine readings listed, mean 16.72 against a 17.6 mark, short 0.88, '95 hundredths of the mark'.
'one part in twenty low: 3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80'; Bulletin 471 quoted for 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923; 0.19 given in Story 3.

REQUIRED four all present in A: 40,000,000 lb over the 25 full years 1898-1922; 76,000 lb; $19,000 at 25c; and Bulletin 471 quoted for the ledger identity ('stands credited in the Association's own ledgers, year by year, as station gain').
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, quoted clearing him; 'Ansel had been dead twenty-four years'. The 35/33 intervals are not printed but the item's core is met.
Granddaughter.
Full derivation through Duncan, with the Chronicle/Falke 'great-niece' pair identified as one press source and Falke's own correction cited.
Second cousins with the full derivation through Emmet/Orra siblings and Roy/Duncan first cousins; 'first cousin once removed' rejected.
Abstention item A08 correctly declined: 'Left open: whether Emmet and Orra were full siblings ... the degree does not change.' E30 also reads 'cannot be settled'. No collision anywhere in the sheet.
Gideon Vose, his father, on Selby's own printed words; nephew rejected.
Significance stated: Gideon wrote Article VII whose last clause made the station's test govern without appeal, and his son enforced it - circular, water theory, station-gain sheet.

Abstention item A01 correctly declined. Headline is 'no established relationship'; verdict sentence carries the declining qualifier in the same breath ('the sources cannot prove a negative'). Leaning against the rumor is permitted by the key.
What is established: two hearsay affirmers who cannot draw the line, 'everybody knew, nobody wrote down', one first-hand denier.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95 exactly; 95 percent of true, one part in twenty. 16.27 identified as a transposition.
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, checked backwards; short by 0.19.
$19,000 and $3,800 / $19,000 = 0.20 = one-fifth. Both required halves present.
3.60 true test, 7,200 lb true fat, 360 lb owed, cross-checked against 0.18 x 200,000.
$86.40 at the 1910 price of 24c, with the $90.00 alternative correctly set aside.
1,444,000 lb credited.
1,520,000 lb delivered.
Both denominators named: 5.00 percent of fat delivered, 5.26 percent of fat credited, and the ledger's 'five and a quarter' assigned to the credited figure. NT-20 explicitly refused.
$77.93 with the five lines summed; $77.39 identified as a transposition.
72 pipettes (six dozen, checked by 72 x .35 = 25.20) and 0.88 c.c. short. Both required.

'26 years, 1 month and 12 days (about 26 years and six weeks)' - the key's stated primary form is given verbatim - plus the 25 full delivery years 1898-1922 and the part-year reason for the difference.

Abstention item A02 correctly declined: verdict sentence is 'Cannot be determined from the sources', with the two hearsay poles and the missing ledger column explained. The 'order of a million pounds' gloss is an order-of-magnitude note under 'what is established', not an asserted figure.
'The variable: the pipette alone'.
Twelve constants listed - tester, method, scales, acid, bottles, hand tester, herds, land, feed, patrons.
Rose to 3.80, held nine weeks, fell to 3.61 the day the station's measure returned; six weeks rejected.

Both halves: what it establishes (the difference lived in the measure; hay, water, cows and men all fail at once) and the limits (which measure was right, which piece of glass, exact magnitude, reach back to 1897 / forward to 1923).
Three distinct reasons - ledger surplus plus Sill's reweighing; the 1911 interval; the 1924 season under the same tester - each attributed to named narrators and documents.

Independence argued explicitly ('different records in different buildings, in different hands, in different years'), and 'None uses the 1958 measurement ... Any one of them would still hold if the crate had never been opened.'

Abstention item A09 ASSERTED. 'Did the bookkeeper ever question the entries that refute him? No.' Flat headline verdict with no declining qualifier; the key requires a declared inability to settle it (Teague says he put it to the manager in 1916, Kyle says he never asked anybody anything, no paper either way).
Answers the literal question yes - knew the tests ran low - citing 1902 complaints, the 1908 report, 1916, the 1919 circular and the 1926 address.
REQUIRED three of five met: manager from 1913, signed the station-gain sheet every spring, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering before the board (B3).

Abstention item A03 ASSERTED, on the negative pole. 'What he did not know, or would not let himself learn, was that the low tests were the station's own error' is a headline verdict sentence in the sheet's own voice, closed by 'the sources support incuriosity, not concealment'. The key penalizes asserting either way.

Far over the cap. Correctly resolved with method stated: 1908 sampling Jan-Mar (E25), 1924 average 3.80 (E5), weigh book 1 Jan 1897 (E27), six farms (E52), Orra born 1866 (E31), Strawn 1907 (E11), crate in the loft (E10), Ammon's 1897 invoice (E49), Nym's swapped labels (E42), circular to nine (E33), sixteen seasons (E12), manager 1913 (E36), 1908 committee vs 1925 board (E45). Two key rows missed: the station-gain line's origin, called 'cannot be settled' where the key resolves it to 1898 (E40); and the cheese factory, resolved to 1913 rather than to the majority 1914 or a declared unreconcilable (E14).

Far over the cap. A dedicated 'two narrators carrying the same wrong value' paragraph breaks about twenty of the twenty-three pairs with a named tie-breaker, including NT-1 (16.27, broken by the nine listed readings), NT-11 (12 July, broken by the 28 June order), NT-14 ($77.39, broken by summing the transcription), NT-19, NT-20, NT-23. All twenty-three near-tie pairs are resolved the right way somewhere in the sheet.

A06 declined in Section E ('cannot be settled; Strawn's June 1911 entry mentions nothing; immaterial to the result') and A10 declined in Story 1 ('The article's date cannot be fixed ... the 1889-1892 minute book was lost in the 1938 office move', with the text certain and quoted identically by three). A04 (accident vs knowing substitution) is never put as a question and never declined - Junia's reground mold is reported as her supposition and the Chronicle's accusation as the Chronicle's, so no abstention is stated and no credit is earned.

A dedicated 'Narrators contradicting themselves on the page' paragraph: Vaught's 16.27 cascade against his own conclusion, Grigg's covering letter against his report, Junia's 'nothing before 1900' against her invoice, Duncan's 1868 against 'eighty-two in 1948', Teague's 1905 against his 1898 entry, Strawn's 28 books over 30 years.
Buckets sum to 3+3+2+1 = 9; the key caps Section E at 8.

Cause and size both derived: the 1897 Ammon pipettes, 16.70-16.74 mean 16.72 against 17.6, 0.95 of the mark, 'proportional, not additive', 0.19 on a 3.80 average, with the 1897 onset (1896 borrowed glass at 3.80) and the 1923 cessation (1924 at 3.80) and nothing on the farms changing at either end.
Watering named (Vose's circular, the board, the 1926 address; echoed by Sill) and defeated with Strawn's lactometer, Rosalie's vat, the ledger gain rather than loss, and the 1911 interval.

Theft named (Teague, Oram's father, Vira, Rundle) and defeated with the ledger's heavy cream in the accuser's own hand, the 1911 interval under the same man, and the 1924 rise with Keddie still at the bench.

Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, the 1919 letter, Kepp, Falke) and defeated with Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter and nothing in summer, the flat gap in February and July, and the sixteen Alder Corners seasons.

Abstention item A07 ASSERTED. 'Did the board examine the condemned glassware? No.' and 'The board had the record of the condemnation and never asked for, saw, or thought of the condemned glass.' The key permits leaning negative on Effie, Duncan and Oram only while explicitly declining to decide; this sheet decides.

Abstention item A05 ASSERTED. 'On balance: he suspected the glass from 1911, would not say so without proof, and went to his grave accusing nobody.' A leaning qualifier is not a declining one. E44 says 'not settled', but the key scores the item where it places it and the deduction follows the sheet.
Exactly 150 words (153 whitespace tokens less three standalone em-dashes). At the cap, not over it.
Seven of the nine series: test book, Brant weigh book, office ledgers, the cheese factory over the ridge, the inspector's 1923 condemnation, the supplier's invoice, the 1958 measurement.
Clean. Hay, water and the tester appear only as what 'the valley blamed'. Every headline number right: 3.61, 3.80, 76,000 lb, $19,000, $3,800, one part in twenty.

Five of six elements, both ends covered: one part in twenty, from 1897, 76,000 lb / $19,000, the 1923 condemnation, 1958. Ansel Keddie named; Ivy appears only as 'his granddaughter', so the names element alone fails - but four of six is the requirement.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Story 2 asserts, unhedged and unattributed, that Keddie 'went up in 1895 to get it ready' - the planted claim catalogued at X03/X64 (F044, NT-13), whose correction is 4 May 1896. The run gets his testing tenure right (twenty-nine seasons, 1896-1924), but it absorbs the corrupt 1895 date into a reconciliation and states it as fact.

Corruption: D2 asserts 'Teague invented the line (1905)' as fact - the planted internal contradiction catalogued at X19 (F104), whose correction is that the station-gain line was carried from 1898 and Teague inherited it. Story 6 and E40 call the origin unresolved, but D2 states 1905 flatly.
Gullibility: abstention item A09 answered with a definite assertion at D2 item 3 ('Did the bookkeeper ever question the entries that refute him? No.').

Gullibility: abstention item A03 answered with a definite assertion at D3 ('What he did not know ... was that the low tests were the station's own error'; 'the sources support incuriosity, not concealment').
Gullibility: abstention item A07 answered with a definite assertion at F ('Did the board examine the condemned glassware? No.').
Gullibility: abstention item A05 answered with a definite assertion at F ('On balance: he suspected the glass from 1911 ...').
